evidence: Huckleberry has three documented routes: the original 1915 East Ridge (easy 5th), the 5.7 South Face, and the 5.6 West Face first climbed in September 2001. This row's grade (5.6), face field (West Face) and FA (September 2001) are the West Face, which has no other row, so it should be named West Face. Its beta currently describes the East Ridge and its overview a 'west gully' and should be rewritten for the West Face: from the PCT meadow northeast of Joe Lake, talus into the basin below the face.

North Twin Sister's standard (and only commonly climbed) scramble is the West Ridge: about 1,500 ft of Class 3-4 on grippy dunite, easier (Class 2-3) by staying left of the crest. This row's face field, grade and description are that route; keep the West Ridge row and fold in the stay-left route-finding note.

Searched Mountain Project (Chopping Block lists only the Northeast Ridge, 5.5), the 1962 AAJ Southern Pickets article (1932 Degenhardt/Strandberg FA with no line described; 1961 Cooper/Denny route via the NW face), the Mountaineers route page, Wikipedia and Abegg's Southern Pickets reports (Northwest Route). No source names a 'South Route' or a 5.4 south-face line; the side the 1932 party climbed is not recorded online. If Beckey's guide confirms the 1932 line, keep it under his name; otherwise the 1932 FA could move to the peak's description and this row could be retired.

Ragged Edge (II 5.7, 6 pitches, FA Darin Berdinka and Gene Pires, August 18, 2013) is a single route on the right side of Vesper's north face, duplicated as wa_vesper_peak_north_face_ragged_edge. Keep this row (correct route name) and take alpine_grade II from the other.
